# Report information

The **main HowMaHiCo report**: one document for both the biologist and the
mass spectrometrist. It opens with a one-screen summary (**At a glance** and
**Red flags**) that answers how many MHC ligands each sample gave and whether
anything needs a closer look, then goes into detail:

* **Identification counts** per Condition, BioReplicate and Sample, by length
  and charge, and the peptide **size distribution**
* the **quality score**: how strongly each sample resembles a genuine MHC
  immunopeptidome, dimension by dimension, plus cross-class contamination
* **overlaps** between replicates and Conditions
* **quantitative reproducibility**: log2(Area) correlation and Area %CV
* sequence **motifs** and the **PTM profile**

The scoring method is in the appendix at the end. The other reports go deeper
into one topic each; see **Where to go next**.

`r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`

**Sample Set:** `r params$SampleSet`

**Data Analysis: ** `r params$DataAnalysisNames`

**Date:**  `r Sys.Date()`

**Code version:** `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")`

```{r child = system.file("rmarkdown", "shared", "setup.Rmd", package = "HowMaHiCo")}
```

```{r overview-data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
window_label <- paste0(shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " AAs")

qc_samples <- qc_samples_from_annotation(
  file.path(params$FolderDocumentation, params$AnnotationFile), params$QCColumn)
threshold_mode <- if (params$ThresholdMode == "qc_relative" && length(qc_samples) > 0)
  "qc_relative" else "default"
if (params$ThresholdMode == "qc_relative" && length(qc_samples) == 0)
  warning("ThresholdMode = 'qc_relative' but no QC samples were found; using default thresholds.")

scores <- score_sample_quality(pep_all, shortpep_range = shortpep_range,
                               mhcclass = params$MHCclass,
                               qc_samples = qc_samples,
                               threshold_mode = threshold_mode)
thresholds_used <- if (threshold_mode == "qc_relative")
  calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(qc_metrics_by_sample(pep_all, shortpep_range, params$MHCclass),
                               qc_samples,
                               thresholds = quality_thresholds_default(params$MHCclass)) else
  quality_thresholds_default(params$MHCclass)

red_flags <- overview_red_flags(scores, thresholds_used, pep_all = pep_all)
```

# At a glance

```{r at-a-glance, echo=FALSE}
n_cat <- table(factor(as.character(scores$category), levels = c("Pass", "Warning", "Fail")))
data.frame(
  Item = c("Samples", "Conditions", "Unique peptides (all lengths)",
           paste0("Unique peptides (", window_label, ")"),
           "Source proteins", "Median quality score (0-100)",
           "Samples Pass / Warning / Fail", "Red flags (High / Medium / Low)"),
  Value = c(length(samples),
            paste0(n_conditions, " (", paste(conditions, collapse = ", "), ")"),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(pep_all$Peptide), big.mark = ","),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(pep_short$Peptide), big.mark = ","),
            format(dplyr::n_distinct(pep_all$Accession), big.mark = ","),
            format(stats::median(scores$composite_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
            paste(n_cat, collapse = " / "),
            paste(table(red_flags$Severity), collapse = " / "))
) |>
  kable(col.names = NULL) |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

# Red flags

```{r red-flags, echo=FALSE}
if (nrow(red_flags) == 0) {
  knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "**No red flags.** Every sample passes the overview checks: no low composite ",
    "score, no quality dimension past its amber threshold, no unusually shallow ",
    "sample and no Condition without biological replicates."))
} else {
  red_flags |>
    dplyr::mutate(Sample = ifelse(is.na(Sample), "(experiment)", Sample)) |>
    kable() |>
    kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

Flags are rule-based and deliberately simple. A flag is a prompt to look, not a
verdict: a low depth or borderline score can have a perfectly good biological
reason, such as a low-input or low-HLA-expressing sample.

# Identification counts

## Total IDs with decoys, DeNovo and contaminants

This evaluation includes all peptides identified, without filtering out peptides that were not assigned to any protein or peptides that could come from contaminant proteins (Accession labeled Cont_). These values are shown below. Some true peptides can be originated from proteins typically assigned as contaminant in proteomics experiments (e.g., actins, keratins, albumins, etc.).

```{r check-ids-global, echo=FALSE}
check_ids_global(pep_all) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = F)
```


```{r counts-all, echo=FALSE}

counts_levels <- c("Peptides", "Sequences", "Proteins")
# display labels (counts_levels stays as the data key: count_lim$Level,
# n_<level> columns, plot_count_mean_sd(level=...))
counts_labels <- c("Peptides", "Sequences", "Parent proteins")

# Counts all peptides
## Sample
counts_all <- pep_all |>
  group_by(Condition, BioReplicate, Sample) |>
  summarise(n_Peptides = n_distinct(Peptide),
            n_Sequences = n_distinct(Sequence),
            n_Proteins = n_distinct(Accession),
            .groups = "drop")

## Condition average
counts_all_mean <-
  counts_all |>
  group_by(Condition) |>
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric),
                   list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                   sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE))),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))
## Condition total
counts_all_total <- pep_all |>
  group_by(Condition) |>
  summarise(n_Peptides = n_distinct(Peptide),
            n_Sequences = n_distinct(Sequence),
            n_Proteins = n_distinct(Accession),
            .groups = "drop")

## BioReplicate per TechReplicate
counts_all_overlap <-
  pep_all |>
  filter(Area != 0) |>
  count(Condition,  Accession, Peptide, Sequence, name = "n_Samples") |>
  mutate(n_Samples = factor(paste0(n_Samples, " Rep."))) |>
  group_by(Condition, n_Samples) |>
  summarise(n_Peptides = n_distinct(Peptide),
            n_Sequences = n_distinct(Sequence),
            n_Proteins = n_distinct(Accession),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  full_join(rename_with(counts_all_total, ~gsub("n_", "total_", .x)), by = "Condition") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(Condition, n_Samples), names_to = "Type_Level", values_to = "n") |>
  separate(Type_Level, sep = "_", into = c("Type", "Level")) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Condition, n_Samples, Level), values_from = "n", names_from = "Type") |>
  arrange(Condition, Level, desc(n_Samples)) |>
  group_by(Condition, Level) |>
  mutate(perc = paste0("", round(100*(n/total), 1), "%"),
         cum = cumsum(n)) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Condition, n_Samples), names_from = Level, values_from = all_of(c("n", "perc", "cum",  "total")))

## Limits for plots
count_lim <- data.frame(Level = c("Peptides", "Sequences", "Proteins"),
                        Limit_mean = c( ceiling((max(counts_all$n_Peptides)*1.2/100))*100,
                                   ceiling((max(counts_all$n_Sequences)*1.2/100))*100,
                                   ceiling((max(counts_all$n_Proteins)*1.3/100))*100),
                        Limit_total = c( ceiling((max(counts_all_total$n_Peptides)*1.2/100))*100,
                                   ceiling((max(counts_all_total$n_Sequences)*1.2/100))*100,
                                   ceiling((max(counts_all_total$n_Proteins)*1.2/100))*100))

### adaptation for running with all way of plotting for the overlaps

npep_ylim <- count_lim[count_lim$Level == "Peptides", "Limit_mean"]
nseq_ylim <- count_lim[count_lim$Level == "Sequences", "Limit_mean"]
nprot_ylim <- count_lim[count_lim$Level == "Proteins", "Limit_mean"]
npep_ylim_total <- count_lim[count_lim$Level == "Peptides", "Limit_total"]
nseq_ylim_total <- count_lim[count_lim$Level == "Sequences", "Limit_total"]
nprot_ylim_total <- count_lim[count_lim$Level == "Proteins", "Limit_total"]
```

## Peptides identified per charge +1 to +4 {.tabset}

```{r charge-proportion-data, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
# Build the charge-state proportion table for a given peptide set (all or selected)
.charge_prop_table <- function(pep) {
  bind_rows(
    pep |>
      get_charge_group() |>
      group_by(Condition, Charge_group) |>
      count_ids() |>
      arrange(Condition, Charge_group),
    pep |>
      get_charge_group() |>
      group_by(Condition) |>
      count_ids() |>
      mutate(Charge_group = "Total")
  ) |>
    mutate(Charge_group = factor(Charge_group, rev(unique(Charge_group)))) |>
    get_proportion_charge()
}

prop_all_condition_charge   <- .charge_prop_table(pep_all)
prop_short_condition_charge <- .charge_prop_table(pep_short)

bp_prop_all_condition_charge <-
  prop_all_condition_charge |>
  plot_charge_proportions(Condition) +
  rotate_x_text(70) +
  ggtitle("Charge proportion all peptides")
bp_prop_short_condition_charge <-
  prop_short_condition_charge |>
  plot_charge_proportions(Condition) +
  rotate_x_text(70) +
  ggtitle("Charge proportion selected peptides")

# check if % > 100, per set (peptides can be reported with multiple charge states)
tmp_prop_total <-
  bind_rows(all = prop_all_condition_charge, short = prop_short_condition_charge, .id = "set") |>
  filter(Charge_group != "Total") |>
  group_by(set, Condition, Level) |>
  summarise(Proportion_Total = sum(Proportion), .groups = "drop")
if(any(tmp_prop_total$Proportion_Total > 1)){
  warning("The total percentage is > 100% in some cases. This may be because some peptides can be reported with multiple charge states (e.g. in Fragpipe)")
}
rm(tmp_prop_total)
```

# Peptide size distribution {.tabset}

**Do the lengths look like MHC ligands?** MHC class I ligands pile up at 8-11
amino acids, usually with a sharp 9-mer peak. MHC class II ligands are longer
and spread more widely, typically 13-17 amino acids. A broad or long-tailed
distribution suggests non-MHC background, such as tryptic or degradation
peptides. The expected window for this run is
`r paste0(shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " AAs")`.

```{r pep-unique-data, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# calculations for plots below
pep_all_unique <- pep_all |>
  select(Peptide, Sequence, PTM, Condition, Length, Mass) |>
  unique()
pep_all_unique_mz <- pep_all |>
  select(Peptide, Sequence, PTM, Condition, Length, Mass, m_z, Charge) |>
  unique()
```

# Quality score

Each sample gets a score from 0 to 100 for how closely it resembles a genuine
MHC immunopeptidome. The composite is a weighted mean of the available
sub-scores: length-window fidelity, motif clarity, low tryptic background,
cross-class contamination, plausible charge states and, where available, mass or
calibration accuracy. **Pass** (70 or more) is a typical immunopeptidome,
**Warning** (40-70) is worth a look, and **Fail** (below 40) suggests a failed
pulldown or a non-MHC sample. Dimensions that are undefined for this dataset
drop out instead of penalising the sample, and the dimensions that replace them
take over: nested-core families stand in for anchor motifs under
`MHCclass = "MHC2"`, and RT/ion-mobility calibration error stands in for mass
error with DIA-NN. The method and thresholds are in the appendix.

`r if (length(qc_samples) > 0) paste0("**QC control samples:** ", paste(qc_samples, collapse = ", "), " (marked with * in plots).") else paste0("No QC control samples tagged (set an annotation <code>", params$QCColumn, "</code> column to enable QC-relative thresholds).")`

**Threshold mode:** `r threshold_mode`

## Composite scores

```{r overview-table, echo=FALSE}
overview <- scores |>
  dplyr::transmute(Sample,
                   QC = ifelse(is_QC, "QC", ""),
                   `Composite score` = composite_score,
                   Category = as.character(category))
overview |>
  kable() |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r plot-composite, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE}

ggprint_rawr(p_quality_composite, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

## Per-metric breakdown

Sub-scores (0-100) for every sample and quality dimension. Red = poor, green =
good; grey = not applicable to this dataset.

```{r plot-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE}
p_quality_heatmap <- plot_quality_heatmap(scores, thresholds_used)
ggprint_rawr(p_quality_heatmap, interactive = interactive_plots)
```

### Raw metrics

The underlying raw values behind each sub-score.

```{r raw-metrics-table, echo=FALSE}
raw_cols <- intersect(thresholds_used$metric, names(scores))
scores |>
  dplyr::select(Sample, dplyr::all_of(raw_cols)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  print_annot()
```

## Cross-class contamination

Peptide-length distribution per sample, highlighting peptides that fall in the
**other** MHC class's length range (MHC-II ligands contaminating an MHC-I pulldown,
or vice versa). A prominent red region indicates cross-class co-enrichment. This is
the `frac_cross_class` sub-score above; it is undefined (and omitted) for custom
length windows.

```{r plot-cross-class, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
p_cross_class_length <- plot_cross_class_length(pep_all, shortpep_range, params$MHCclass)

```

## Unique identifications across BioReplicates

```{r upset-tables, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
upset_table_pep <-
  pep_all |>
  mutate(Condition = as.character(Condition)) |>
  distinct(Condition, Peptide, .keep_all= FALSE) |>
  nest(Condition = Condition) |>
  group_by(Condition)  |>
  summarize(n_Peptide = n_distinct(Peptide), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(n_Condition = nrow(Condition)) |>
  mutate(Conditions= paste(Condition, collapse = ", ")) |>
  select(Conditions, n_Condition, n_Peptide) |>
  rbind(pep_all |>
          group_by(BioReplicate) |>
          summarize(Conditions = paste("Total", unique(BioReplicate)),
                    n_Peptide = n_distinct(Peptide), .groups = "drop",
                    n_Condition = 1) |>
          select(-BioReplicate)) |>
  rbind(pep_all |>
          summarize(Conditions = "Total",
                    n_Peptide = n_distinct(Peptide), .groups = "drop",
                    n_Condition = 1) )

upset_table_prot <-
  pep_all |>
  mutate(Condition = as.character(Condition)) |>
  distinct(Condition, Accession, .keep_all= FALSE) |>
  nest(Condition = Condition) |>
  group_by(Condition)  |>
  summarize(n_ProteinGroup = n_distinct(Accession), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(n_Condition = nrow(Condition)) |>
  mutate(Conditions = paste(Condition, collapse = ", ")) |>
  select(Conditions, n_Condition, n_ProteinGroup) |>
  rbind(pep_all |>
          group_by(BioReplicate) |>
          summarize(Conditions = paste("Total", unique(BioReplicate)),
                    n_ProteinGroup = n_distinct(Accession), .groups = "drop",
                    n_Condition = 1) |>
          select(-BioReplicate)) |>
  rbind(pep_all |>
          summarize(Conditions = "Total",
                    n_ProteinGroup = n_distinct(Accession), .groups = "drop",
                    n_Condition = 1))

upset_table_unique <-
  full_join(upset_table_pep[upset_table_pep$n_Condition == 1, ] |>
               select(-n_Condition),
            upset_table_prot[upset_table_prot$n_Condition == 1, ]  |>
               select(-n_Condition),
             by = "Conditions") |>
  rename_with(.fn =function(x) gsub("n_", "Unique_", x)) |>
  rename(Condition = Conditions)

upset_table_unique |>  kable() |>   kable_paper("hover", full_width = F)
```

# Condition pairwise overlap  {.tabset}


```{r overlap-pairwise-data, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8}
# calculations needed for Condition, Bioreplicate, and sample-wise overlap and uniqueness
npep_all_overlap <- pep_all |>
  dplyr::group_by(Condition) |>
  dplyr::summarise(total_Peptides = dplyr::n_distinct(Peptide), .groups = "drop")

#complete condition comparison with same condition in each side
# all pairs plus the self-comparisons; condition_pairs() returns just the
# self-comparisons when the subset has a single Condition (combn() would error)
comp_condition_replicated <- condition_pairs(conditions, self = TRUE)



pep_overlap <-
  data.frame(n_Overlap = sapply(comp_condition_replicated,
                                function(x) count_intersect(pep_all, variable = "Peptide",
                                                            cond1 = x[1], cond2 = x[2])),
             n_Total = sapply(comp_condition_replicated,
                                function(x) count_merged(pep_all, variable = "Peptide",
                                                            cond1 = x[1], cond2 = x[2]))) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Comparison") |>
  separate(Comparison, into = c("Cond1", "Cond2"), sep = "_vs_") |>
  mutate(prop_Overlap_Total = round(n_Overlap/n_Total, 3)) |>
  # Add total IDs per condition and the proportion of overlap
  full_join(npep_all_overlap |>  select(Condition, total_Peptides) |>
              unique() |>
              rename(n_Peptides_Cond1 = total_Peptides),
            by = c("Cond1" = "Condition")) |>
  full_join(npep_all_overlap |>  select(Condition, total_Peptides) |>
              unique() |>
              rename(n_Peptides_Cond2 = total_Peptides),
            by = c("Cond2" = "Condition")) |>
  mutate(prop_Overlap_Cond1 = round(n_Overlap / n_Peptides_Cond1, 3),
         prop_Overlap_Cond2 = round(n_Overlap / n_Peptides_Cond2, 3))  |>
  mutate(Cond1 = factor(Cond1, levels = conditions), #reorder levels
         Cond2 = factor(Cond2, levels = conditions))
```

```{r corr-log2area-data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
pep_all_log2area_br  <- get_mat_log2area(pep_all, PeptideID, BioReplicate)

prot_all_log2area_br <- get_mat_log2area(pep_all, ProteinFirst, BioReplicate)
## short peptides

pep_short_log2area_br  <- get_mat_log2area(pep_short, PeptideID, BioReplicate)

prot_short_log2area_br <- get_mat_log2area(pep_short, ProteinFirst, BioReplicate)
```

## All peptides

```{r plot-corr-all, echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=8, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
# Matrix of log2(Area)
# Guard first: with no quantified peptide at all (Areas absent or every Area 0)
# get_mat_log2area() yields a 0-row matrix, and cor() on it errors ("'x' is
# empty") before the all-NA check further down could report the problem.
corr_log2area_all <- if (nrow(pep_all_log2area_tr) == 0) NULL else
  cor(pep_all_log2area_tr, method = "pearson", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

#setup limits
corrarea_lim <- if (is.null(corr_log2area_all) || all(is.na(corr_log2area_all))) c(0, 1) else
  c(floor(min(corr_log2area_all, na.rm = TRUE)), ceiling(max(corr_log2area_all, na.rm = TRUE)))

corrarea_mid <- ifelse(all(corrarea_lim == c(-1,1)), 0, 0.7)
if(all(corrarea_lim == c(-1,1))){
  corrarea_breaks <- seq(-1, 1, 0.2)
}else {
  corrarea_breaks <- seq(0, 1, 0.1)
}


if(is.null(corr_log2area_all) || all(is.na(corr_log2area_all))){
  warning("Correlation plot cannot be generated: no non-missing Log2Area correlation. ",
          "Maybe the Areas were not included, or they are all zero.")
}else{
  p_corr_log2area_all <-
  corr_log2area_all |>
  plot_corr() +
  ggtitle("Log2Area correlation for all peptides")

ggprint_rawr(p_corr_log2area_all, interactive = TRUE)
}


```

# PTM profile {.tabset}

The modification tokens are translated to readable names (`translate_ptm()`),
because each search engine writes them differently:

- **FragPipe** reports the monoisotopic **delta mass** behind a position and
  residue -- `2M(15.9949)`
- **DIA-NN** reports the **UniMod accession** -- `(UniMod:35)`
- **PEAKS** reports the modification **name** -- `Oxidation (M)` -- and keeps the
  delta mass in the peptide string instead; some exports use a bracketed delta
  mass (`[+15.99]`)

Those are all the same modification, and all of them are shown as `Oxidation`
below. A token that matches no known modification is left exactly as the search
engine wrote it. `pep_all$PTM` itself keeps the raw token.

# Appendix: quality-score method

Each dimension, its scoring direction, the thresholds in force, and its weight in
the composite. In `default` mode the green/amber thresholds are literature-informed
constants; in `qc_relative` mode green is the QC-sample median and amber is that
median relaxed by 20%.

```{r methods-table, echo=FALSE}
thresholds_used |>
  dplyr::transmute(Metric = label, Direction = direction,
                   `Green (=100)` = round(green, 3), `Amber (=50)` = round(amber, 3),
                   Weight = weight) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

- **Length in window / 9-mer fraction** — the hallmark of an HLA immunopeptidome:
  peptides concentrate in the expected ligand-length window (here
  `r paste0(shortpep_range[1], "-", shortpep_range[2])` AAs) and, for HLA-I, peak at 9-mers.
  With `MHCclass = "MHC1_mouse"` the metric counts **8- and 9-mers** instead, since
  murine H-2 ligands peak at both (H-2Kb favours 8-mers, H-2Db 9-mers), and its
  green/amber thresholds are raised accordingly.
- **Anchor motif clarity** — Shannon information (bits) at the P2 and PΩ anchor
  positions of 9-mers; sharp anchors indicate genuine allele-restricted ligands.
  Computed from the data only (no binding predictor or HLA typing). Defined for
  MHC-I only: class-II ligands have no fixed-length anchor register, so this is
  `NA` for `MHCclass = "MHC2"`.
- **Nested-core families** — the class-II motif dimension, and the substitute for
  anchor clarity there. Fraction of in-window ligands sharing a 9-mer (the length
  of the MHC-II binding core) with another ligand of the same sample. Class-II
  peptides are trimmed into ragged, length-variable families around one core, so a
  genuine HLA-II immunopeptidome is dominated by nested sets while a background or
  contaminant set is not. No alignment, register guess or binding predictor is
  involved. It carries the anchor metric's weight for `MHCclass = "MHC2"` and is a
  weight-0 diagnostic for MHC-I, where some nesting is normal but not the primary
  signal. Its class-II thresholds are **provisional** — prefer
  `ThresholdMode = "qc_relative"` when the experiment carries QC controls.
- **Tryptic background (long peptides)** — fraction of peptides *outside* the
  length window ending in K/R. Because some HLA-I alleles legitimately use K/R as a
  C-terminal anchor, the overall C-terminal K/R fraction is reported only as a
  low-weight diagnostic; the scored signal isolates tryptic contamination in the
  long-peptide tail.
- **Cross-class contamination** — fraction of peptides in the *other* MHC class's
  length range, outside the current window (MHC-II co-enrichment in an MHC-I run, or
  vice versa). Low weight (a small tail is biologically normal) and `NA` for custom
  length windows.
- **Charge 1+/2+ (class I) / Charge 2+ to 4+ (class II)** — short HLA-I
  ligands ionise predominantly as 1+/2+, while the longer HLA-II ligands carry
  more basic residues and come mostly as 2+ to 4+. The metric counts the
  class-appropriate charges; the class-II cut-offs (green 0.80, amber 0.60) are
  **provisional**.
- **Depth** — unique peptides / in-window peptides / source proteins; scored only
  in `qc_relative` mode (absolute yield is not comparable without per-input
  normalisation).
- **Median |ppm|** — mass accuracy; `NA` (dropped) for DIA-NN, which reports a
  dummy `ppm = 0`. Mass error is an MS2-level DDA metric: DIA-NN's `Precursor.Mz`
  is the *library* value and the report carries no observed precursor m/z, so a
  real ppm cannot be recovered from it.
- **Median |RT − predicted RT| and |1/k0 − predicted 1/k0|** — the DIA analogue of
  mass accuracy. DIA-NN reports a predicted retention time and ion mobility per
  precursor, and the deviation from them measures how well the run matches the
  library/model. Both are `NA` (dropped) for FragPipe and PEAKS, which carry no
  prediction — the mirror image of `ppm` being dropped for DIA-NN. The cut-offs
  are **instrument- and gradient-dependent**, so `qc_relative` mode is the
  meaningful way to use them.
